newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down, investors see no incentive.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down, investors see no incentive.

text.p: * Main index down by 0.88 points to 3,193.68
Manila shares closed slightly lower on Friday in the absence of fresh incentives for investors to pit in fresh money, traders said.
"Our fundamentals are good but there's really no money. There is no real incentive to invest so the index was just moving within a tight band," said Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Securities.
The main index dropped by 0.03 percent, or 0.88 points, to 3,193.68 at Friday's close of trading.
Though the index ended slightly down, gainers outpaced losers 73 to 40 with 70 issues were unchanged.
"Most of the buys were on speculative and secondary issues so that there was really no effect on the index," said Rudsend Alpay, trader at Lippo Securities.
Traders said the market will continue to move sideways next week until the U.S. Federal Reserve decides on interest rates.
